title: Canonical completed coefficient pullback comparison respects finite quotient projections
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient data $p,a,q,k_0,k$, $\ell\ne p$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $\mathcal O_E$, $\varpi_E$ and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ ($n\ge1$) [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_{T,n}=(A_n)_T$ and $R_T=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}=\varprojlim_nB_{T,n}$ for $T=X,Y$, with projections $\pi_{n,T}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the inverse image and ring isomorphisms $c_n:g^{-1}B_{Y,n}\to B_{X,n}$ and $c_R:g^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], where $\pi_{n,X}c_R=c_ng^{-1}(\pi_{n,Y})$.

Let $P_g=Lg^*$ be the completed integral pullback [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Let $\kappa_{R_Y}:g^{-1}R_Y\to P_gR_Y$ be the specified map [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b). Let $\lambda_R:P_gR_Y\to g^{-1}R_Y$ be the CANONICAL multiplication/completeness comparison of [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback]: on a flat-term K-flat model [def-pc-kflat-complex] it is induced on the entire strict quotient cone by the finite maps $x\otimes b\mapsto c_n^{-1}(b)x$, the inverse-image comparison for that cone, and the inverse of the canonical completeness map. At finite level let $\lambda_n:Lg_n^*B_{Y,n}\to g^{-1}B_{Y,n}$ be $x\otimes b\mapsto c_n^{-1}(b)x$; its inverse is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. The coefficient sheaf $R_Y$ and its reductions are derived complete constructible coefficient objects [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible]. Let $\rho_n:P_gR_Y\to\operatorname{Res}_n Lg_n^*B_{Y,n}$ be the specified projection of the completed pullback model, using the canonical reduction $R_Y\otimes^L A_n\cong B_{Y,n}$ and restriction of scalars [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients].

Then the canonical comparison, including its actual cone maps, satisfies
$$\lambda_R\circ\kappa_{R_Y}=\mathrm{id}_{g^{-1}R_Y},\qquad \kappa_{R_Y}\circ\lambda_R=\mathrm{id}_{P_gR_Y},$$
$$\operatorname{Res}_n(\lambda_n)\circ\rho_n=g^{-1}(\pi_{n,Y})\circ\lambda_R,$$
and consequently, for $\theta_R=c_R\circ\lambda_R$,
$$\pi_{n,X}\circ\theta_R=\operatorname{Res}_n(c_n\circ\lambda_n)\circ\rho_n.$$
The equalities are compatible with the specified maps $A_{n+1}\to A_n$ before passing to the derived inverse limit. When $X=Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ for a finite-type $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$ and $g=g_Y$, this is the canonical $\lambda$ and $\theta_{\mathcal O_E}$ used in [def-weil-constant-weil-structure](3), not an arbitrary isomorphism $P_gR_Y\cong g^{-1}R_Y$. This is a statement about coefficient pullback and its reduction projections, without a claim about Frobenius on cohomology.

source.place: Tag 03D6, definition-pushforward (module pullback by tensor); derived.tex Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit (quotient cone). Agent-formulated normalization of the canonical multiplication/completeness comparison in lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback for coefficient objects, needed in blueprint prop-cohomological-finiteness, Proof Step 7.

proof.text: Write $F=g^{-1}$ with its $R_X$-module action transported through $c_R$. By [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image](1)--(3), this is site relabelling and preserves products: its product comparison has components $F(\operatorname{pr}_n)$. This applies to $R_Y$-modules too: sectionwise relabelling preserves the action map and the module identities, and transport through $c_R$ changes only the action. The exact descended module functor is the one specified in [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Choose the flat-term K-flat resolution $q:P\to R_Y$ used there, by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and set $P_n=P\otimes_{R_Y}B_{Y,n}$, $\gamma_n(x)=x\otimes1$ and $\tau_n=1\otimes r_{n,Y}$. These are the actual quotient arrows of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations].

source.place: Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit; setup using the specified quotient complexes

proof.text: For every complex $M$ of $B_{Y,n}$-modules define $\mu_{n,M}:g_n^*M\to FM$ by $x\otimes b\mapsto c_n^{-1}(b)x$. The balancing relation gives $\mu((a x)\otimes b)=c_n^{-1}(b)a x=\mu(x\otimes c_n(a)b)$, so this induces a map of sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Its inverse is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$: the composites are $x\mapsto x$ and $x\otimes b\mapsto c_n^{-1}(b)x\otimes1=x\otimes b$. These formulas commute with restrictions and differentials and are natural in $M$. For $M=B_{Y,n}$ this is exactly $\lambda_n$. Writing $D_n=F\operatorname{Res}_nP_n$ and $C_n=\operatorname{Res}_ng_n^*P_n$, we get chain isomorphisms $\mu_n:C_n\to D_n$. They are $R_X$-linear because $\pi_{n,X}c_R=c_nF\pi_{n,Y}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image].

source.place: Tag 03D6, definition-pushforward; explicit multiplication inverse on module pullback

proof.text: The maps $\mu_n$ commute strictly with tower transitions. Indeed [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image](3) gives $F(r_{n,Y})c_{n+1}^{-1}=c_n^{-1}r_{n,X}$; thus both routes on $x\otimes b$ give $c_n^{-1}(r_{n,X}b)F(\tau_n)x$. The tensor formulas descend from presheaves to sheaves as in Step 2. Put $V=\prod_n\operatorname{Res}_nP_n$, $H=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:V\to V)[-1]$ and $C=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_nC_n\to\prod_nC_n)[-1]$. In these cones $d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s)a,da)$, with degree $i$ equal to the product in degree $i-1$ plus that in degree $i$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The product of the $\mu_n$, followed by the inverse product comparison of Step 1, applied to BOTH coordinates gives a chain isomorphism $L:C\to FH$: it intertwines $d$ and $1-s$, and hence the displayed cone differentials. Its inverse applies the inverse maps in both coordinates. If $e_n:H\to\operatorname{Res}_nP_n$ and $e'_n:C\to C_n$ are projection from the second coordinate, then $F(e_n)L=\mu_ne'_n$ as chain maps.

source.place: Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit; the strict commuting square on both cone coordinates

proof.text: The products and cones just used represent the derived products and limits: [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] applies to the completed module sheaves, and [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence](2) identifies their termwise products with derived products. By [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined], $C$ represents the specified $P_gR_Y$. By [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison], the strict-tower cone construction descends with its maps and all its projections. Thus the chain isomorphism $L$ of Step 3 gives the inverse-image comparison for the whole quotient cone; the comparisons do not choose a new cone map in a triangulated category.

source.place: Tag 08TC and lemma-products (Tag 07KC); strict-tower normalization supplied by the cited nodes

proof.text: Let $a:P\to H$ be $z\mapsto(0,(\gamma_nz)_n)$. The equality $\tau_n\gamma_{n+1}=\gamma_n$ makes it a chain map, and $e_na=\gamma_n$. Put $\eta=[a][q]^{-1}:R_Y\to H$ in the derived category. By [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible](2), $R_Y$ is derived complete. Apply [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] with $L=E$ and $K=R_Y$. Its explicit zero-shifted-component description identifies this particular $\eta$ with its canonical completeness map (using the multiplication unitor $P\otimes_{R_Y}R_Y\cong P$). The isomorphism assertion of that node therefore makes $\eta$ an isomorphism, independent of the K-flat representative.

source.place: Bhatt--Scholze Proposition 3.5.1 and Definition 3.5.2, p. 24; L=E canonical strict augmentation normalization

proof.text: By [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b), $\kappa_{R_Y}=[\widetilde\theta][Fq]^{-1}$, where $\widetilde\theta(z)=(0,(F\gamma_n(z)\otimes1)_n)$. Step 2 gives $\mu_n(F\gamma_n(z)\otimes1)=F\gamma_n(z)$, and the product comparison has these same components. Therefore $L\widetilde\theta=F(a)$ on BOTH cone coordinates. Consequently $L\kappa_{R_Y}=F(\eta)$. The canonical comparison specified in the item is precisely $\lambda_R=F(\eta)^{-1}L$, the multiplication/cone comparison followed by inverse completeness. It follows by cancellation that $\lambda_R\kappa_{R_Y}=1$; since $L$ and $F(\eta)$ are isomorphisms, also $\kappa_{R_Y}\lambda_R=1$. This identifies the actual specified morphisms.

source.place: Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit; equality of the zero-first-coordinate augmentations

proof.text: Let $h_n:P_n\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{Y,n}$ be the canonical derived reduction identification. Clause 2 of [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible] supplies its invertibility. To identify its arrows, $R_Y[0]$ is itself K-flat: tensoring a complex with this unit complex is isomorphic to the same complex by multiplication, so it preserves acyclicity [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Apply [lem-weil-integral-reduction-tower-well-defined](1)--(2) to $q:P\to R_Y$ and $1:R_Y\to R_Y$, using $R_Y\otimes B_{Y,n}\cong B_{Y,n}$. This gives $h_n[\gamma_n][q]^{-1}=\pi_{n,Y}$ and $h_n[\tau_n]=r_{n,Y}h_{n+1}$. Explicitly $h_n$ is induced by $q\otimes1$ followed by multiplication; it is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings](1), since both $P$ and $R_Y[0]$ are K-flat. Thus the transition and quotient identities can already be checked on these chain maps. By the specified model projection in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], $\rho_n=g_n^*(h_n)e'_n$. Naturality of the multiplication maps of Step 2 gives $\lambda_ng_n^*(h_n)=F(h_n)\mu_n$.

source.place: Tag 03D6 and the quotient-arrow normalization of lem-weil-integral-reduction-tower-well-defined

proof.text:
All maps in the following calculation are in the single $R_X$-module derived category, with finite-level maps restricted along $\pi_{n,X}$. Steps 3, 5 and 7 give
$$\operatorname{Res}_n(\lambda_n)\rho_n=F(h_n)\mu_ne'_n=F(h_ne_n)L.$$
Since $h_ne_n\eta=h_n[\gamma_n][q]^{-1}=\pi_{n,Y}$, invertibility of $\eta$ yields
$$F(h_ne_n)L=F(\pi_{n,Y})F(\eta)^{-1}L=F(\pi_{n,Y})\lambda_R.$$
This is the required projection identity. Using $\pi_{n,X}c_R=c_nF(\pi_{n,Y})$ [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], composition with $c_n$ gives
$$\pi_{n,X}\theta_R=\operatorname{Res}_n(c_n\lambda_n)\rho_n.$$
Transition compatibility holds before the derived limit: it is the strict square of Step 3, with the compatible quotient arrows of Step 7; in the coefficient model $P=R_Y$ these are exactly $r_{n,Y}$ and $r_{n,X}$. Thus no claim of uniqueness from limit projections is needed.

source.place: Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit; compose the explicit cone-projection equalities

proof.text: For $X=Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $g=g_Y$, [def-weil-constant-weil-structure](1)--(3) uses the same $c_n$ and the limit map $c_R$. Its $\lambda$ is understood with the canonical normalization stipulated in the item: finite multiplication, the entire quotient-cone comparison and inverse canonical completeness. Steps 2--6 construct exactly that composite on the chosen resolution. Hence its $\theta_{\mathcal O_E}=c_R\lambda$ is the $\theta_R$ calculated here. This final specialization uses no cohomological Frobenius assertion.
